tool_input.description: Inspect label and input elements in both snapshots

result:
I wrote the test and checked it both ways. It passes on the before snapshot and fails on the after snapshot, which reports that the Username label (`... form:nth-child(2) > div:nth-child(1) > label:nth-child(1)`) has text-align `'center'` where `'start'` was expected.

The test finds the Username and Password labels by their `for` attribute, which is present in both snapshots. For each one it asserts that the computed `text-align` is `start` and that the label text's left edge is at x=56, within 1 px. I didn't read the before values out of the snapshot directly, because ad-hoc Python wasn't allowed in this session. I used the detector's before boxes (x=56) and the browser's default `start`, and the test passing on the before snapshot confirms both values match it.

I left the Sign Up button out on purpose. The design intent says centering it was the point of the change, so asserting on it would flag an intended change as a regression.
